title: The Wedding Bride
novel:
Ted went to the cinema and saw a movie called "[[The Wedding Bride|The Wedding Bride]]." To his horror, it was based on his failed relationship with Stella — written by Tony, the man who had stolen her.

In the film, the Ted character was the [[villain|villain]]: a selfish, [[neurotic|neurotic]] man who could not commit. The Tony character was a [[hero|hero]], noble and brave. Every scene [[humiliated|humiliate]] the real Ted.

He sat in the dark theater, [[cringing|cringe]] as strangers laughed at his fictional self. Marshall tried to comfort him. "It's just a movie," he said.

"It's my life," Ted whispered, "and they made me the [[bad guy|bad guy]]."

Barney, of course, loved it. He [[quoted|quote]] lines from the film for weeks.

But Ted found a strange [[relief|relief]] in the end. The movie was a [[distorted|distort]] version of the truth, but it let him see his story from the outside. He had made mistakes. He had been [[selfish|selfish]]. Seeing it on screen — even [[exaggerated|exaggerate]] — helped him forgive himself, and finally let Stella go.

The Wedding Bride.en: a movie title in the show

villain.en: the bad character in a story

hero.en: the main good character in a story

quote.en: to repeat words someone else said

relief.en: the good feeling when worry ends

distort.en: changed so it is no longer true

exaggerate.en: made larger or worse than reality
